newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan prosecutors continue raids on DKB.
newsitem.headline: Japan prosecutors continue raids on DKB.

text.p: Japanese state prosecutors said on Wednesday that they were continuing to search Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) premises as part of their investigation connected with the scandal at Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Deputy Chief Prosecutor Kunihiro Matsuo told reporters that prosecutors raided DKB at several locations on Wednesday, after earlier raids on Tuesday, but did not elaborate on where they were.
About 100 investigators were involved in Wednesday's raids, he added. He said prosecutors were investigating DKB in connection with the alleged violation of the Commercial Code by Nomura.
Jiji news agency reported earlier on Wednesday that prosecutors had raided the homes of current and former DKB executives.
Japanese newspapers have also reported that the bank is likely to announce the resignations of some of its top management before its board of directors meet on Friday.
DKB has not commented on allegations that it provided questionable loans to the racketeer at the centre of the Nomura Securities payoff scandal, Ryuichi Koike.
Koike and his younger brother Yoshinori Koike were arrested last week on suspicion of taking about 50 million yen in illegal payments from Nomura.
Two former Nomura executives and a third senior Nomura official have also been arrested in the case.

The Commercial Code bans companies from making payments to "sokaiya" racketeers, who extort money by threatening to disrupt shareholders meetings or offering to protect the meetings from disruptions from rival sokaiya.
